draft.title: Speaking to an audience
card: Voice
A speaker can change volume (how loud), pace (how fast), tone (the mood in the voice) and emphasis (stressing certain words). Each change shapes how the audience feels about the words.
Pause
A pause is a short silence. It can build suspense before an important point, or give listeners a moment to think about what they just heard.
Body
Gesture is the use of hands and body to support the words. Eye contact is looking at people in the audience. Eye contact helps a speaker connect with listeners and seem sincere.
A speaker chooses these techniques to suit the purpose. A slow, quiet voice can calm an audience, while a fast, loud voice can show excitement or urgency.
draft.remember: A speaker's voice and body are choices that shape how the audience receives the message.

a.q: Ravi is giving a speech. He stops speaking for two seconds just before his main point. What is the most likely effect of this pause?
opts: It builds attention before the main point
It shows he has forgotten his speech
It makes the audience feel calmer and relaxed
It connects him to listeners through eye contact
a.why: A pause creates a short silence that makes listeners wait and focus on what comes next. Eye contact is a different technique, so the last option names the wrong one.
a.clue: Think about what listeners do during a silence before a big point.

b.q: Mia is speaking at assembly about a lost class pet. She wants the school to feel gentle sympathy. Which choice would best suit her purpose?
opts: A soft, slow voice with a sad tone
A fast, loud voice with an excited tone
A flat voice with no pauses or emphasis
A loud voice with sharp, jabbing gestures
b.why: A soft, slow voice and a sad tone match the mood of sympathy. A fast, loud, excited voice suits urgency or excitement, which would not match a gentle message.
b.clue: Match the voice to the feeling Mia wants the audience to have.

a.best: It builds attention before the main point

b.best: A soft, slow voice with a sad tone
